You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Rust (reading the book)
G2: Go (did the tour)
G3: machine learning (unfinished course)
G4: AWS certification (course only, no exam)
G5: Terraform authoring
G6: official team lead title

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Copying the 'Learning: Rust, Go' line as skills
T2: Turning the unfinished AWS Cloud Practitioner course into a certification or the unfinished ML course into ML skills
T3: Calling him Tech Lead / Team Lead as a job title (project tech lead only; acting lead only in notes)
T4: Claiming Terraform authoring
T5: Failing to condense: keeping duplicated Älvgrind sections, hobbies, gymnasium, band
T6: Dropping qualifiers like 'Vue (a little)', 'Tailwind (some)'
T7: Old cover letter is to his current employer and says he is at Sjöbris

# OUTPUT 1: CV
OSKAR
Full-Stack Engineer | TypeScript / React
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Full-stack developer with 12 years of professional experience building web and mobile applications.
Strongest in frontend development with React and TypeScript, with professional experience delivering
backend services using Node.js, NestJS and PostgreSQL. Recent work includes fintech onboarding
identity verification, secure document upload and an incremental backend migration. Experienced as a
project tech lead and acting team lead, with hands-on delivery of identity verification and secure
ID-document upload flows in a fintech onboarding product.
CORE SKILLS
Frontend: React, TypeScript, Angular, React Native
Backend: Node.js, NestJS, Express, Laravel, Apollo Server
Databases and ORM: PostgreSQL, TypeORM, Prisma
Cloud and messaging: AWS ECS, S3, Lambda, SQS; Firebase Cloud Messaging
Other: WordPress, GraphQL (maintained an Apollo Server BFF), Python (basic), YAML
LANGUAGES
English
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Full-Stack Developer | Älvgrind Fintech AB 2021–Present
• Develop onboarding features using React, TypeScript, NestJS and PostgreSQL, with AWS services.
• Built a BankID identity verification step for onboarding; see Selected Projects for details.
• Delivered a secure ID-document upload flow; see Selected Projects for details.
• Contributed to an incremental migration of the onboarding backend from Express to NestJS, moving
route by route behind the same API gateway.
• Maintained an Apollo Server BFF.
• Acted as team lead for four months in 2024 during the lead’s parental leave, including 1:1s and sprint
planning.
Developer | Sjöbris Digital Agency AB 2018–2021
• Delivered client web and mobile projects using Angular, React, React Native, Laravel and
WordPress.
• Served as project tech lead and built most of a React Native ferry-ticket app in a two-developer team.
The app supports ticket purchase and offline ticket display and has approximately 50,000 downloads.
Developer | Nordkust Media 2014–2018
• Worked on newspaper websites.
SELECTED PROJECTS
BankID Identity Verification Flow 2022
• Built a new onboarding identity-verification step using Swedish BankID, with QR-code and
same-device flows through a provider SDK.
• A/B tested with 10% of traffic before full rollout; onboarding conversion increased from 61% to 74%.
• Technologies: React, TypeScript, NestJS, PostgreSQL, AWS ECS.
Secure Document Upload 2023
• Implemented customer ID-document uploads (up to 20 MB) using S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV
virus scanning in Lambda, and scan-status handling through SQS into PostgreSQL.
• Technologies: AWS S3, Lambda, SQS, NestJS, PostgreSQL.
Express to NestJS Migration 2021–2022
• Contributed to an incremental onboarding-backend migration, moving routes from Express to
NestJS behind the same API gateway.
• Gave a meetup talk about the migration in 2022.
• Technologies: Node.js, Express, NestJS, TypeORM, Prisma.
Ferry Ticket Mobile App 2019–2020
• Tech lead in a two-developer team; built most of a React Native app for buying and showing ferry
tickets offline. The app has approximately 50,000 downloads.
• Technologies: React Native, TypeScript, Node.js, Firebase Cloud Messaging.
Home Assistant Integrations | Personal project 2022–Present
• Built two small custom home-automation integrations, published on GitHub with approximately 40
stars combined.
• Technologies: Python (basic), YAML.
LEADERSHIP EXPERIENCE
Acting Team Lead 2024
• Covered the team lead role for four months during parental leave, conducting 1:1s and sprint
planning.

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Verdane Care team,
I’m applying for the Full-Stack Engineer role on the Patient Experience squad. I’m a
full-stack developer with 12 years of professional experience, strongest in React and
TypeScript, and with hands-on experience building Node.js services and working with
PostgreSQL. Verdane Care’s focus on patient-facing tools, accessible design and privacy by
default makes this role especially compelling.
In my current role at Älvgrind Fintech, I build onboarding features using React, TypeScript,
NestJS and PostgreSQL. I built a BankID identity-verification flow that was A/B tested
before rollout; onboarding conversion increased from 61% to 74%. I also implemented a secure
ID-document upload flow using S3 presigned URLs, virus scanning in Lambda and scan-status
handling through SQS. These projects have given me practical experience building end-to-end
features where usability and careful handling of sensitive information matter.
I’ve also contributed to an incremental migration of an onboarding backend from Express to
NestJS, and maintained an Apollo Server BFF. Earlier, as project tech lead in a two-developer
team, I built most of a React Native ferry-ticket app, which now has around 50,000
downloads. I’d be glad to bring this mix of frontend strength, backend delivery and hands-on
product experience to Verdane Care’s patient-facing work.
Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how my
experience could contribute to the Patient Experience squad.
Best regards,
Oskar

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
